reference: Network Flows: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications
natural_language_example: A logistics team moves product through a directed transfer network. Some nodes have supply, some nodes have demand, and intermediate nodes must conserve flow. Each directed arc has a per-unit shipping cost and a hard capacity. The planner chooses continuous nonnegative arc flows to satisfy every node balance exactly while minimizing total shipping cost. This is not a vehicle-routing, facility-location, or fixed-charge network design problem.
